Slides and video recording of the talk "A Long-Term Archival Pipeline for the Forschungsdatenplattform" by Moritz Mähr and Moritz Twente from Stadt.Geschichte.Basel, held at the Museum für Kommunikation in Bern on October 15th, 2025. Using a large historical research project as its example, the talk explains why long-term preservation is needed: project funding ends, FAIR data needs good metadata, researchers need persistent identifiers to cite sources, and lightweight hosting cannot handle large files. It then presents omeka2dsp, a pipeline that moves cultural heritage data from Omeka S into the DaSCH data infrastructure. The slides cover differences between the two data models, the metadata crosswalk from Dublin Core to DaSCH properties, validation with Python scripts, and versioned updates that keep ARK identifiers stable. They also compare the DSP REST API with the DSP-Tools bulk import and finish with lessons learned and recommendations for projects that plan to archive with DaSCH.

## Learning outcomes

After working through this resource, users will be able to:

- explain why research projects need a long-term preservation strategy and persistent identifiers
- describe the main steps of an archival pipeline from Omeka S to DSP, including data model mapping and metadata crosswalks
- compare the DSP REST API and DSP-Tools for first deposits and later updates
- apply good practices: plan transformations early, validate thoroughly, document mapping decisions
